## renv — package version locking
To lock exact package versions for reproducibility, run once from the R console
after all packages are installed and working:
```r
# renv::init()     # first time: initialise and snapshot
# renv::snapshot() # after adding/updating packages
# renv::restore()  # collaborators run this to install exact same versions
```
Do NOT run renv::init() mid-analysis — do it when the project is stable and
ready for GitHub. The renv.lock file should be committed to the repository.

## functions
```{r functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# function to remove rows with n number of NA's
delete.na <- function(DF, n=0) {
  DF[rowSums(is.na(DF)) <= n,]
}
```


## define universal variables
```{r define_universal}

## random seed — Clusterize and rrarefy are stochastic; re-set before each so
## results are reproducible even when chunks are run individually
rand_seed <- 20261022

stud_pat <- "RS_surface"

## All inputs, outputs, and plots live in the '2026 RS eDNA' folder.
## here::here() resolves the absolute path from the .Rproj root, so this
## works both when knitting and when running chunks interactively in RStudio.
dir         <- paste0(here::here("2026 RS eDNA"), "/")
dada2_path  <- paste0(dir, "Dada2_output/")   # DADA2 pipeline output files
export_file <- ""                              # CSV exports → dir
out_file    <- ""                              # summary outputs → dir
summary_file<- ""                              # manuscript tables → dir

# name for the main filtered data CSV saved at the end
export_name <- paste0(stud_pat, "_filtered_data_all.csv.gz")   # gzipped (fwrite compresses by extension) to stay under GitHub's 100 MB limit

## set some other universal variables

####  !!!! need to be in alphabetical order - tabs in sam_file should match these names too !!!!! also have "type"" column
primers<-c('18smini',"euka02")  # 18S_V9 and 18S_V7 only; CO1 and 12S excluded
n_primers<-length(primers)
## must be in alphabetical order
minboots<-c("insect",50,70,90)  # for getting all data minboots and insect data
min_insect_score<-0.80# set minimum score for insect taxa score
###################           filtering parameters
## filter based on occurance in samples
min_samples_include<-3  # remove 97% clusters present in < this number of samples (only occurrence filter in the pipeline)

## filter based on proportion in samples
sam_sum_prop_cut<-0.00005 ## remove 97% clusters with less than this proportion of total sample reads per primer (applied to cluster totals in filter chunk)
      # examples 10 million reads if 0.0001 then remove SV with lesst than 100 reads (remove ~25-50% SV) .......OK  USED
      # examples 10 million reads if 0.001 then remove SV with lesst than 1000 reads (remove ~60-80% SV) .......conservative
     # logic - if very low percent in sample samples, then likely errors.

## decontam: numeric proxy for below-detection-limit DNA concentration
## Samples recorded as "<0.50 ng/mL" in the Excel are read as NA by openxlsx.
## decontam requires all concentration values to be positive numbers (> 0),
## so below-detection samples are assigned this proxy value instead of NA.
## It means "DNA present but unquantifiable" — adjust if your detection limit differs.
decontam_conc_low <- 0.01  # ng/µl proxy for samples with conc recorded as "<0.50 ng/mL"

## contamination removal: minimum number of blank samples an SV must appear in
## (reads > 0) to be removed as a contaminant.  Used in decontam_check together
## with decontam (combined method) — SVs are removed if flagged by EITHER rule.
blank_n_remove <- 3
blank_ratio_min <- 1  # blank rule also needs: share of blank reads / share of sample reads >= this
                      # (stops abundant real taxa that spill into blanks from being removed)

## non-marine / terrestrial taxa: one row per rule (rank, name); an ASV is removed
## if its taxonomy at that rank equals name. Add new terrestrial taxa to this file.
non_marine_file <- "Red_sea_non_marine_taxa.csv"

## sample filters (true samples only; blanks and controls kept)
sample_read_cut      <- 1000  # remove sample x primer with fewer reads after all filters
                              # (failed amplifications <= 701 reads; lowest real sample 2990)
require_both_primers <- TRUE  # keep only samples passing sample_read_cut for every primer

## set minumum number for rarefaction -- some samples usually have very few reads, partucularly for cores
#    !!!!!!! estimate run script and look at rare_mins,..... then choose!!!  !!!!!!!! -- 1000 to 5000 ?????????
min_num_rarefaction<-5000

#  stil run but NO longer used - now based on occurance within each miseq run - at later time.

#####################
##   for summary tables
###  change from old to new names
primers_summary_old<-c("euka02",'18smini')
primer_names<-data.frame( "Primer1"=c("18S_V7","18S_V9"), "primer_pair"= primers_summary_old, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
primers_summary<-c("18S_V7","18S_V9")
minboots_summary<-c("70")  # character to match taxa_assign column after separate()


############
################### set file path and name of sample data
## each primer should have own sheet with name matching primers
## primer sheets first then location sheet (1 row per each sample location), then other sheets with relevent data
sam_file_path <- paste0(dir, "RS_surface_sample_data_all.xlsx")

## number of columns in the primers specific sheets, should be the same for all primer pairs, 
num_sample_cols<-10  ####
##

```


## import data
Sample data excel sheet should include sheet for each primer pair - samples id column then other info
then a sheet with locations, then a sheet with other sample relevant data
It then imports data from DADA2 pipeline
```{r import}
# sample data -- will need Quality control !!! make sure sample_se make sense
sheets <- openxlsx::getSheetNames(sam_file_path)
sam_dat <- lapply(sheets,openxlsx::read.xlsx,xlsxFile=sam_file_path)  # mes1<-sam_dat[[2]]   names(mes1)  names(sam_dat)
names(sam_dat) <- sheets   # add name to each list

##    move to next .Rmd - nothing to do here
# locations<-sam_dat[[n_primers+1]]  # isolate locations  ! double check depending
sample_dat<-sam_dat$sample_data # isolate other data
##

sam_dat <-sam_dat[1:n_primers]   # keep only primer sample data
sam_dat <- lapply(sam_dat, function(df) mutate_at(df, .vars="sample_ID", as.character))  # make sure sample_ID is character
sample_sam<-bind_rows(sam_dat, .id = 'id')  # names(sample_sam)   ## bind al primer pair data into single datagrame

#  import taxonomy assigned to sequences  
# summary, seqtab and taxass    list.files()    unique(sam$type)
## list.files with explicit path — avoids setwd() side-effects in Rmd
## full.names=TRUE returns the complete path so read functions work regardless of WD
f_tax <- list.files(path = dada2_path, pattern = paste0(stud_pat, ".*taxass.*\\.csv"), full.names = TRUE)
f_sum <- list.files(path = dada2_path, pattern = paste0(stud_pat, ".*summary\\.csv"),  full.names = TRUE)
f_rds <- list.files(path = dada2_path, pattern = paste0(stud_pat, ".*seqtab\\.rds"),   full.names = TRUE)
##   import all data into lists            names(sum)  names(tax_list)
###  may need to add  "sample1" to last column ????
tax_list<-setNames(lapply(f_tax, read.csv), tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f_tax)))  # mes1<-tax_list[[2]]  names(mes1)


## make sure tax_list names match primer names and sample_sam
intersect(primers, names(sam_dat))
# intersect(primers, names(tax_list))

# get index for insect taxonomy assigned and add taxonomy comparable to assigntaxonomy from DADA2
tax_list_insect_num<-grep("insect", names(tax_list))
# fix taxonomy of insect    match insect name to dada2 nameing
for (i in tax_list_insect_num){
     tax_list[[i]]<-tax_list[[i]] %>% 
       # mes1<-tax_list[[9]]   %>% 
       dplyr::rename(Superkingdom=superkingdom, Kingdom=kingdom,Phylum=phylum, Class=class, Order=order, Family=family, Genus=genus, Species=species ) %>% 
       mutate(X = taxID) %>%  ## add to match seq from tax assign
        select(-representative,-taxID,-taxon,-rank) %>%
       mutate_if(is.factor, as.character) %>% 
       mutate_at(vars(Superkingdom:Species), list(~na_if(., ""))) %>% # convert blank to NA
       mutate_at(vars(Superkingdom:Species), list(~ifelse(!is.na(score) &  score < min_insect_score, NA, .))) %>%  ## min score turn taxa blank   -  min_insect_score !is.na(score) &
       select(-score, -contains("sample1")) ## 3 remove score
     }
 ## mes1<-tax_list[[9]]       names(mes1)
       



# get summary of reads from filter steps of DADA2

summar<-setNames(lapply(f_sum, read.csv), tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f_sum)))  # names(summar) mes1<-summar[[1]] 
## get seqtab tables from dada2  -- sample_id are row names and colnames are SV sequence
sv_list<-setNames(lapply(f_rds, readRDS), tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f_rds))) # mes1<-sv_list[[2]]  row.names(mes1)
```

## tidy data

```{r tidy}
#######################################
# tidy     ! DADA2  summary tables !    table from dada2 pipe

## make column name lower for sample information
sample_dat<-sample_dat %>% 
    rename_all(tolower)


#######   tidy summary data     #################
## add column for primer and sampple_id  mes<-summar[[1]]  mes<-mes$sample_id
for (i in seq_along(summar)){
  summar[[i]]["sample_num"] <- rownames(summar[[i]]) }  #  
## most are numbers so need to convert to sample_id from sample sheets, switching between sample_num and sample_id need to be chekced

# bind into dataframe
sum2<-bind_rows(summar, .id = 'names(sum)')
names(sum2)[1]<-"study_primer"
## get name of primer and clean up - NEED TO CHECK each time !!!!
sum2 <-sum2 %>% 
  rename_all(tolower) %>% 
  mutate(primer=study_primer) %>%
  mutate(primer=gsub("^.*?_","",primer)) %>%  # remove everything before first "_"
  mutate(primer=gsub("_[^_]+$","",primer)) %>%   # remove after last "_"
   mutate(primer=gsub("^.*?_","",primer)) %>% 
  mutate(primer=gsub("_","",primer)) %>%   # remove any "_"
  mutate(study_primer=gsub("_[^_]+$","",study_primer))


##############################################################################
#########    tidy miseq specific data    then   combine with summary   ######### 
#   names(sam)  unique(sam$primer)  unique(sum2$primer)

# add total number of sequences per sample to each primer sheet
sample_sam<-sample_sam[,c(1:num_sample_cols)]# keep only common columns  names(sample_sam) 
sam2<-sample_sam %>%
  rename_all(tolower) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(primer=id) %>% 
  mutate(sample_num=as.character(sample_num)) %>% 
  left_join(sum2[,7:9]) %>% # keep only nonchim,id,primer
  dplyr::rename(reads_per_sample_dada=nonchim)   ### reads after DADA2 filters

###### set up sample data-sam2 to merge with tax data
# set sample list for each primer  use sam2 by primer
sam_list<-split(sam2,f=sam2$primer) # names(sam_list)   # split data from each primer into list

#  get index to call column names of sample types   x<-sam_list[[1]]
##      !!!!!!!!!    need to sort samples in alpabetical order    !!!!! see lines below
## for most miseqs we just use sample_num, during pipe this is ordered as character, so need to be aware
##  need for next step of indexing columns to sepcify sample type
sam_list<- lapply(sam_list, function(x) { 
  row_number_original<-c(1:length(as.numeric(row.names(x)))) 
  x$sample_num<-as.character(x$sample_num)
  x<-arrange(x,sample_num)
  row.names(x)<-NULL
  row_number<-c(1:length(as.numeric(row.names(x)))) # make index for choose columns of SVs - SV from DADA2 arranges columns by !!!alphabet !!!!! - need to arrage accordingly
  x<-cbind(x,row_number,row_number_original)    })
# replicate to match list with primers and nboots.
 sam_list<-rep(sam_list, each=length(minboots))
 #####
 
## make lists for each sample type, needed for filtering  x<-sample_index_list[[6]]  unique(sam2$type) x<-sam_list[[3]]
sample_index_list<- lapply(sam_list, function(x) { 
  x<-x$row_number[x$type=="sample"]     })
#
blank_index_list<- lapply(sam_list, function(x) { 
  x<-x$row_number[x$type=="extraction blank" | x$type=="pcr blank"]     })  # x<-blank_index_list[[3]] 
#
positive_index_list<- lapply(sam_list, function(x) { 
  x<-x$row_number[x$type=="positive control" | x$type=="mock"]     })
#
all_index_list<- lapply(sam_list, function(x) { 
  x<-x$row_number    })

### make SV list into LIST of dataframes ######################################
dat<-purrr::map(sv_list, data.frame)
# make rownames a column, rownames were sample identification, which we use sample number  -  mes<-dat[[1]]  mes$sample_num
dat<-purrr::map(dat, function(x) rownames_to_column(x, var="sample_num"))  #  mes<- rownames(dat[[3]]) names(dat) all_index_list[[3]]
```


## get cluster seqs (cluster)
  updated Sept 2024 from arctic surface - seqateurs::cluster_otus no longer worked
```{r cluster}

 cluster_dat <- dat# make list
#. i<-1
for (i in seq_along(dat)){

 cluster_sub<- cluster_dat[[i]]   # remove sample number
 cluster_sub<-cluster_sub[,-1]

asv_sequences <- colnames(cluster_sub)
seqs <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(asv_sequences)

set.seed(rand_seed + i)   # reproducible clustering
otus <- DECIPHER::Clusterize(
    seqs,
    cutoff = 0.03,  # use `cutoff = 0.03` for a 97% OTU
    method = "overlap",
    includeTerminalGaps = FALSE,
    penalizeGapLetterMatches = NA,
    minCoverage = 0.5,
    maxAlignments = 100,
    invertCenters = FALSE,
    processors = 4) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sequence = asv_sequences)  %>%
    dplyr::group_by(cluster) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cluster_size = n_distinct(sequence)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

cluster_dat[[i]]<-otus

}
```

## begin filtering

```{r filter}
####    begin filter SV based on # samples and blanks
####################################################################################
      #  mes1<-dat3[[11]]  names(mes1)  mes2<-dat3[[2]]   # names(dat4)  mes0<-tax_list[[2]]  names(tax_list)
      #  hist(apply(mes1[,samples_index],1,function(x) length(which(x>0)))) # sum SV's per sample
      #  mes2<-mes1[apply(mes1[,samples_index],1,function(x) (length(which(x>0)))>=min_samples_include),]


#### remove 97% clusters present in < min_samples_include samples  - loop through all lists
dat4<-dat3
after_n_occurance_per_sample <- vector("list", length(names(dat4)))# make dummy list
names(after_n_occurance_per_sample) <- primers_minboot
after_n_occurance_per_sample1 <- vector("list", length(names(dat4)))# make dummy list mes<-after_n_occurance_per_sample[[1]]
names(after_n_occurance_per_sample1) <- primers_minboot
after_n_occurance_SVsam <- vector("list", length(names(dat4)))  # ASVs per sample after this step
names(after_n_occurance_SVsam) <- primers_minboot

### start loop
for (i in seq_along(dat4)){   ##  i<-9   names(dat4[[9]])  names(dat4)
  
        mes1<-dat4[[i]]
        # occurrence counted per 97% CLUSTER (any of its ASVs present in a sample),
        # so a single-sample ASV is kept if its cluster occurs in >= min_samples_include samples
        clust_reads <- rowsum(as.matrix(mes1[, sample_index_list[[i]]]), mes1$cluster)
        clust_n_samp <- rowSums(clust_reads > 0)
        mes2<-mes1[clust_n_samp[as.character(mes1$cluster)] >= min_samples_include,]
   
        after_n_occurance_per_sample[[i]]<-length(row.names(mes2))
        after_n_occurance_per_sample1[[i]]<-apply(mes2[,all_index_list[[i]]], 2, sum) # all_index_list was changed apr23,2020
        after_n_occurance_SVsam[[i]]<-apply(mes2[,all_index_list[[i]]], 2, function(x) sum(x > 0))
             dat4[[i]]<-mes2
      }     #  mes2<-dat4[[16]]  mes1<-dat4[[16]]  names(mes2)  names(mes1)

#  find sample that is not common between index list and dat3 - common error   i<-18
#    setdiff(as.character(all_index_list[[i]] ), as.character(gsub("X_", "", names(dat3[[i]])[1:96] ) )  )

###################################################
#### remove SVs with very low proportional reads in samples (likely sequencing errors)
#### contamination removal (blank-based + decontam) is applied in the decontam_check chunk

dat_filt <- dat4   # copy for downstream filtering   names(dat4)  names(dat2[[1]])

# summary lists for sam_sum_prop filter step (populated below)
after_min_sample_filt        <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_min_sample_filt) <- primers_minboot
after_min_sample_filt1       <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_min_sample_filt1) <- primers_minboot
after_min_sample_filt_SVsam  <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_min_sample_filt_SVsam) <- primers_minboot

# summary lists for contamination filter step (populated in decontam_check)
after_blank_filt        <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_blank_filt) <- primers_minboot
after_blank_filt1       <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_blank_filt1) <- primers_minboot
after_blank_filt_SVsam  <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_blank_filt_SVsam) <- primers_minboot

for (i in seq_along(dat_filt)) {    #  i<-1
  mes1 <- dat_filt[[i]]

  sv_sum <- apply(mes1[, sample_index_list[[i]]], 1, sum)

  # proportion is calculated on the 97% CLUSTER total, not the single ASV —
  # one taxon is often split over many small ASVs that would each fail an
  # ASV-level cutoff (removed ~80% of named taxa when applied per ASV)
  clust_sum <- ave(sv_sum, mes1$cluster, FUN = sum)
  mes1$sam_sum_prop <- clust_sum / sum(sv_sum)

  # remove clusters with < sam_sum_prop_cut proportion of total sample reads —
  # low-level noise / tag-jumps
  mes2 <- mes1[mes1$sam_sum_prop > sam_sum_prop_cut, ]
  mes2 <- dplyr::select(mes2, -sam_sum_prop)

  dat_filt[[i]] <- mes2

  # summary stats for this step
  after_min_sample_filt[[i]]       <- length(row.names(mes2))
  after_min_sample_filt1[[i]]      <- apply(mes2[, all_index_list[[i]]], 2, sum)
  after_min_sample_filt_SVsam[[i]] <- apply(mes2[, all_index_list[[i]]], 2, function(x) sum(x > 0))
}
     
 # convert all factors to characters
 #  and
 # remove taxonomy that are not assigned to any taxonomy  !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
  after_taxa_clean <- vector("list", length(names(dat_filt)))# for calc of lost SVs
  names(after_taxa_clean) <- primers_minboot
   after_taxa_clean1 <- vector("list", length(names(dat_filt)))# for calc of lost reads
   names(after_taxa_clean1) <- primers_minboot
   after_taxa_clean1_SVsam <- vector("list", length(names(dat_filt)))# for calc of lost reads
   names(after_taxa_clean1_SVsam) <- primers_minboot
 #  mes1<-dat_filt[[10]]

    for (i in seq_along(dat_filt)){ 
    dat_filt[[i]]<-dat_filt[[i]] %>%   # i<-1
      tidyr::unite(lineage, Superkingdom:Species,sep=";",remove=F) %>%
      # keep ASVs named at CLASS or below (Class, Order, Family, Genus or Species not NA).
      # Was family-or-below, which removed ~65% of reads incl. real meiofauna, fish,
      # mangrove (Lamiales) and seagrass (class-only Magnoliopsida). Decided 2026-10-22.
      filter_at(vars(Class:Species), any_vars(complete.cases(.)))    %>%
      mutate_if(is.factor, as.character) %>% 
      select(-lineage)
    
        # get data for summary
      after_taxa_clean[[i]]<-length(row.names(dat_filt[[i]]))# sum rows, count sum >0
      after_taxa_clean1[[i]]<-apply(dat_filt[[i]][,all_index_list[[i]]], 2, sum) 
      after_taxa_clean1_SVsam[[i]]<-apply(dat_filt[[i]][,all_index_list[[i]]], 2, function(x) sum(x > 0)) 
     }
# x<-dat_filt[[11]]     filter_at(vars(b, c), any_vars(complete.cases(.))   any_vars(!is.na(.))

  
```



## decontam contamination removal (combined method) + blank-count filter
Removes SVs flagged by decontam OR (present in ≥ `blank_n_remove` blanks AND a larger share
of blank reads than of sample reads, ratio ≥ `blank_ratio_min`).
Updates `dat_filt` in place — run before `sum_by_taxa`.
Install decontam if needed: BiocManager::install("decontam")

```{r decontam_check}
library(decontam)

## Contamination removal: decontam combined method (frequency + prevalence) OR
## (present in ≥ blank_n_remove blanks AND blank_ratio >= blank_ratio_min).
## blank_ratio = (SV reads / all blank reads) / (SV reads / all sample reads).
## Runs at summary minboot (minboots_summary).
## Updates dat_filt in place; run before sum_by_taxa.
##
## Concentration source: extr_dna_conc. from sample_data tab (extracted DNA, pre-PCR).
##   - Frequency test uses TRUE SAMPLES ONLY — blanks ignored (B. Callahan, decontam #88).
##   - Prevalence test uses the neg vector independently of concentration.

tax_cols    <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
decontam_idx <- which(grepl(paste0(";", minboots_summary, "$"), primers_minboot))

# sample_id → extracted DNA concentration (lowercased in tidy chunk)
conc_lookup <- sample_dat %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_id, extr_dna_conc.) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

## ── 1. run decontam ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
decontam_res <- purrr::map(decontam_idx, function(i) {
  primer_id <- primers_minboot[i]
  meta      <- sam_list[[i]] %>%
    dplyr::left_join(conc_lookup, by = "sample_id")

  # samples × SVs matrix (rows = samples)
  sv_mat <- t(as.matrix(dat_filt[[i]][, all_index_list[[i]]]))

  neg  <- meta$type %in% c("extraction blank", "pcr blank")
  # suppressWarnings: "<0.50 ng/mL" strings → NA by design
  conc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(meta$extr_dna_conc.))
  conc[is.na(conc) & !neg] <- decontam_conc_low   # below-detection samples
  conc[is.na(conc) &  neg] <- decontam_conc_low   # blanks (not in sample_dat)

  contam_df <- isContaminant(sv_mat, conc = conc, neg = neg,
                             method = "combined", threshold = 0.1)
  contam_df$primer_taxassign_id <- primer_id
  contam_df
})
names(decontam_res) <- primers_minboot[decontam_idx]

## ── 2. prepare plot data (built pre-filter so all SVs are visible) ────────────

## p1_data: decontam scores stacked across primers for facet histogram
p1_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(decontam_res, function(df, nm) {
  dplyr::mutate(df, primer = nm)
})

## decontam_plot_data: inputs for decontam::plot_frequency (one entry per primer)
decontam_plot_data <- lapply(seq_along(decontam_idx), function(j) {
  idx  <- decontam_idx[j]
  nm   <- names(decontam_res)[j]
  meta <- sam_list[[idx]] %>%
    dplyr::left_join(conc_lookup, by = "sample_id")
  neg  <- meta$type %in% c("extraction blank", "pcr blank")
  conc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(meta$extr_dna_conc.))
  conc[is.na(conc)] <- decontam_conc_low
  sv_mat <- t(as.matrix(dat_filt[[idx]][, all_index_list[[idx]]]))
  # plot_frequency requires character column names — assign row names explicitly
  # (default integer row names can be lost through matrix coercion)
  colnames(sv_mat) <- as.character(rownames(dat_filt[[idx]]))
  flagged <- which(decontam_res[[nm]]$contaminant)
  top_svs <- if (length(flagged) > 0)
    head(flagged[order(decontam_res[[nm]]$p[flagged])], 5) else integer(0)
  # short taxonomy label for each top SV: "Genus Species (p=X)"
  taxon_labels <- if (length(top_svs) > 0) {
    paste0(
      dat_filt[[idx]][top_svs, "Genus"], " ",
      dat_filt[[idx]][top_svs, "Species"],
      " (p=", round(decontam_res[[nm]]$p[top_svs], 3), ")"
    )
  } else character(0)
  list(nm = nm, sv_mat = sv_mat, conc = conc, neg = neg,
       top_svs = top_svs, taxon_labels = taxon_labels)
})

## ── 3. diagnostic tables (keep for future reference) ─────────────────────────

## SVs flagged by decontam — full taxonomy + p-value
decontam_flagged <- purrr::imap_dfr(decontam_res, function(df, nm) {
  idx     <- which(primers_minboot == nm)
  flagged <- which(df$contaminant)
  if (length(flagged) == 0) return(NULL)
  sv_sum  <- apply(dat_filt[[idx]][flagged, all_index_list[[idx]]], 1, sum)
  dat_filt[[idx]][flagged, tax_cols] %>%
    dplyr::mutate(primer_taxassign_id = nm,
                  sample_reads        = sv_sum,
                  decontam_p          = df$p[flagged]) %>%
    dplyr::select(primer_taxassign_id, all_of(tax_cols), sample_reads, decontam_p)
}) %>% dplyr::arrange(primer_taxassign_id, desc(sample_reads))

## SVs present in ≥ 1 blank — shows how blank count varies across taxa
blank_n_taxa <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(decontam_idx), function(j) {
  idx <- decontam_idx[j]
  nm  <- primers_minboot[idx]
  if (length(blank_index_list[[idx]]) == 0) return(NULL)
  blank_mat <- dat_filt[[idx]][, blank_index_list[[idx]], drop = FALSE]
  n_blanks  <- rowSums(blank_mat > 0)
  sv_sum    <- apply(dat_filt[[idx]][, sample_index_list[[idx]]], 1, sum)
  bl_sum    <- rowSums(blank_mat)
  dat_filt[[idx]] %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(tax_cols)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(primer_taxassign_id = nm,
                  sample_reads        = sv_sum,
                  blank_reads         = bl_sum,
                  n_blanks            = n_blanks,
                  blank_ratio         = round((bl_sum / sum(bl_sum)) / (sv_sum / sum(sv_sum)), 2)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_blanks >= 1)
}) %>%
  tidyr::separate(primer_taxassign_id, into = c("primer_pair", "minboot"),
                  sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::select(primer_pair, all_of(tax_cols), sample_reads, blank_reads, n_blanks, blank_ratio) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(primer_pair, desc(n_blanks), desc(sample_reads))

cat("\ndecontam flagged", nrow(decontam_flagged), "SVs\n")
decontam_flagged

cat("\nSVs appearing in ≥ 1 blank (n_blanks column; blank_n_remove =", blank_n_remove, "):\n")
blank_n_taxa

## ── 4. apply combined filter to dat_filt (all primer × minboot combinations) ─
## decontam is run at summary minboot; flagged SV row names are matched by row
## name across all minboot thresholds for the same primer pair.

# build a named list: primer_pair → SV row names flagged by decontam
decontam_sv_names <- setNames(
  lapply(seq_along(decontam_idx), function(j) {
    idx     <- decontam_idx[j]
    flagged <- which(decontam_res[[j]]$contaminant)
    row.names(dat_filt[[idx]])[flagged]
  }),
  sapply(primers_minboot[decontam_idx], function(x) strsplit(x, ";")[[1]][1])
)

# per primer × minboot: ASVs / sample reads removed by each contamination rule
contam_breakdown <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(contam_breakdown) <- primers_minboot

for (i in seq_along(dat_filt)) {
  primer_pair <- strsplit(primers_minboot[i], ";")[[1]][1]

  # decontam-flagged SVs for this primer (from summary minboot run)
  dc_sv <- if (primer_pair %in% names(decontam_sv_names))
    decontam_sv_names[[primer_pair]] else character(0)

  # SVs present in ≥ blank_n_remove blanks AND relatively more abundant in blanks
  # than in samples, for this primer × minboot
  if (length(blank_index_list[[i]]) > 0) {
    blank_mat <- dat_filt[[i]][, blank_index_list[[i]], drop = FALSE]
    n_blanks  <- rowSums(blank_mat > 0)
    bl_sum    <- rowSums(blank_mat)
    sam_sum   <- rowSums(dat_filt[[i]][, sample_index_list[[i]], drop = FALSE])
    bl_ratio  <- (bl_sum / sum(bl_sum)) / (sam_sum / sum(sam_sum))  # Inf if 0 sample reads
    bl_sv     <- row.names(dat_filt[[i]])[which(n_blanks >= blank_n_remove & bl_ratio >= blank_ratio_min)]  # which(): drops NaN when blanks have 0 reads
  } else {
    bl_sv <- character(0)
  }

  # OR logic: remove if flagged by either method
  remove_sv   <- union(dc_sv, bl_sv)

  # record what each rule removed (ASVs present in this data set only)
  rn       <- row.names(dat_filt[[i]])
  sam_rd   <- rowSums(dat_filt[[i]][, sample_index_list[[i]], drop = FALSE])
  in_dc    <- rn %in% dc_sv
  in_bl    <- rn %in% bl_sv
  grp      <- list(decontam_only = in_dc & !in_bl, blanks_only = in_bl & !in_dc,
                   both = in_dc & in_bl, total_removed = in_dc | in_bl)
  contam_breakdown[[i]] <- data.frame(
    primer_taxassign_id = primers_minboot[i],
    rule                = names(grp),
    ASVs                = sapply(grp, sum),
    sample_reads        = sapply(grp, function(g) sum(sam_rd[g])),
    pct_sample_reads    = sapply(grp, function(g) 100 * sum(sam_rd[g]) / sum(sam_rd)))
  keep        <- !row.names(dat_filt[[i]]) %in% remove_sv
  dat_filt[[i]] <- dat_filt[[i]][keep, ]

  # update summary stats (used by summary_table chunk)
  after_blank_filt[[i]]       <- length(row.names(dat_filt[[i]]))
  after_blank_filt1[[i]]      <- apply(dat_filt[[i]][, all_index_list[[i]]], 2, sum)
  after_blank_filt_SVsam[[i]] <- apply(dat_filt[[i]][, all_index_list[[i]]], 2,
                                       function(x) sum(x > 0))
}

cat("\nContamination filter applied: decontam OR (≥", blank_n_remove, "blanks AND blank ratio ≥", blank_ratio_min, ")\n")
cat("SVs remaining per primer (minboot =", minboots_summary, "):\n")
for (nm in primers_minboot[decontam_idx]) {
  cat(" ", nm, ":", after_blank_filt[[nm]], "SVs\n")
}
```

## decontam plot 1: p-value distribution
Run `decontam_check` first. One panel per primer.
Good signal = spike near 0; flat = decontam could not find a signal.
```{r decontam_plot1}
ggplot2::ggplot(p1_data, ggplot2::aes(x = p)) +
  ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ primer, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "decontam p-value distribution (combined method, threshold = 0.1)",
    x     = "decontam score (p)",
    y     = "count"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))
```

## decontam plot 2: one panel per top-flagged SV, proportion vs DNA concentration
Contaminants should show higher proportion at LOW concentration.
Blue circles = true samples; red triangles = blanks (plotted at x = -4).
Facets = individual SVs (Genus Species + decontam p-value); primers with no
flagged SVs are skipped with a message.  Single ggplot object → always renders.
```{r decontam_plot2}
p2_data <- purrr::map_dfr(decontam_plot_data, function(d) {
  if (length(d$top_svs) == 0) {
    message(d$nm, " \u2014 no contaminants flagged, skipping")
    return(NULL)
  }
  # drop samples with zero total reads (avoids 0/0 in proportion)
  keep     <- rowSums(d$sv_mat) > 0
  sv_sub   <- d$sv_mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  conc_sub <- d$conc[keep]
  neg_sub  <- d$neg[keep]
  log_conc <- ifelse(neg_sub, log10(1e-4), log10(conc_sub + 1e-4))
  total    <- rowSums(sv_sub)

  # one row per sample per top SV — each SV becomes its own facet panel
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(d$top_svs), function(k) {
    sv_reads <- sv_sub[, d$top_svs[k]]
    data.frame(
      taxon    = d$taxon_labels[k],
      log_conc = log_conc,
      prop     = ifelse(total > 0, sv_reads / total, NA_real_),
      type     = ifelse(neg_sub, "blank", "sample")
    )
  })
})

ggplot2::ggplot(p2_data, ggplot2::aes(x = log_conc, y = prop,
                                       colour = type, shape = type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(sample = "steelblue", blank = "red")) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values  = c(sample = 16,          blank = 17)) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ taxon, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title  = "Top 5 decontam-flagged SVs: proportion vs extracted DNA concentration",
    x      = "log10(extracted DNA conc, ng/\u00b5l)",
    y      = "proportion of reads",
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top",
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))
```


## remove non-marine / terrestrial taxa
Removes ASVs whose taxonomy matches a rule in `non_marine_file` (rank + name, e.g.
Class = Insecta, Species = Homo sapiens). Moved here from the analysis script
(2026-10-23) so it is part of the summary tables and applies to every taxon, not
only taxa with a row in the traits file. Updates `dat_filt` in place.

```{r non_marine}
non_marine <- read.csv(paste0(dir, non_marine_file), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

after_marine_filt        <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_marine_filt) <- primers_minboot
after_marine_filt1       <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_marine_filt1) <- primers_minboot
after_marine_filt_SVsam  <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(after_marine_filt_SVsam) <- primers_minboot
non_marine_removed       <- vector("list", length(primers_minboot))
names(non_marine_removed) <- primers_minboot

for (i in seq_along(dat_filt)) {
  mes1 <- dat_filt[[i]]
  # rule matched by each ASV (first match), NA = keep
  hit <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(mes1))
  for (r in seq_len(nrow(non_marine))) {
    m <- is.na(hit) & mes1[[non_marine$rank[r]]] %in% non_marine$name[r]
    hit[m] <- paste(non_marine$rank[r], non_marine$name[r], sep = ": ")
  }

  sam_rd <- rowSums(mes1[, sample_index_list[[i]], drop = FALSE])
  non_marine_removed[[i]] <- data.frame(primer_taxassign_id = rep(primers_minboot[i], length(hit)),  # rep(): some slots have 0 ASVs
                                        rule = hit, sample_reads = sam_rd) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(rule)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(primer_taxassign_id, rule) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(ASVs = dplyr::n(), sample_reads = sum(sample_reads), .groups = "drop")

  dat_filt[[i]] <- mes1[is.na(hit), ]

  after_marine_filt[[i]]       <- nrow(dat_filt[[i]])
  after_marine_filt1[[i]]      <- apply(dat_filt[[i]][, all_index_list[[i]]], 2, sum)
  after_marine_filt_SVsam[[i]] <- apply(dat_filt[[i]][, all_index_list[[i]]], 2, function(x) sum(x > 0))
}

non_marine_removed <- dplyr::bind_rows(non_marine_removed) %>%
  tidyr::separate(primer_taxassign_id, into = c("primers", "taxa_assign"), sep = ";") %>%
  dplyr::filter(taxa_assign %in% minboots_summary) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::transmute(non_marine, rule = paste(rank, name, sep = ": "), reason),
                   by = "rule") %>%
  dplyr::relocate(reason, .after = rule) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(primers, desc(sample_reads))
non_marine_removed
```

## remove low-read samples
True samples with < `sample_read_cut` reads after all filters are removed, per primer;
if `require_both_primers`, a sample must pass for every primer (per minboot). Blanks and
controls are kept. Moved here from the analysis script (2026-10-23). Also writes
`RS_surface_dropped_samples.csv` (every metadata sample, with drop reason and reads).

```{r sample_filter}
# some sample IDs carry an XML artifact prefix ('xml:space="preserve">') in both
# the metadata and primer sheets; strip it for matching and for the export
clean_id <- function(x) stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_remove(x, '^xml:space[^>]*>'))

samp_reads <- dat_filt_taxa_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "sample") %>%
  dplyr::distinct(primer, minboot, sample_id, sample_sum_after_filt) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pass_reads = sample_sum_after_filt >= sample_read_cut)

samp_keep <- samp_reads %>%
  dplyr::group_by(minboot, sample_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n_pass = sum(pass_reads), n_seq = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(keep = if (require_both_primers) n_pass == n_primers else n_pass > 0)

## drop table for every metadata sample (summary minboot)
sample_drops <- sample_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("rep", sample_id, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(sample_id_clean = clean_id(sample_id), habitat, area, year) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    samp_reads %>%
      dplyr::filter(minboot %in% minboots_summary) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(primer_names, by = c("primer" = "primer_pair")) %>%
      dplyr::transmute(sample_id_clean = clean_id(sample_id), Primer1,
                       reads = round(sample_sum_after_filt)) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Primer1, values_from = reads, names_prefix = "reads_"),
    by = "sample_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    samp_keep %>%
      dplyr::filter(minboot %in% minboots_summary) %>%
      dplyr::transmute(sample_id_clean = clean_id(sample_id), keep, n_pass),
    by = "sample_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(keep)  ~ "not in sequence data",
    keep         ~ "retained",
    n_pass == 0  ~ paste0("< ", sample_read_cut, " reads, all primers"),
    TRUE         ~ paste0("< ", sample_read_cut, " reads, one primer"))) %>%
  dplyr::select(-keep, -n_pass) %>%
  dplyr::rename(sample_id = sample_id_clean) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(status != "retained", habitat, sample_id)

cat("\nSamples by status and habitat (minboot", minboots_summary, "):\n")
print(table(sample_drops$status, sample_drops$habitat))
sample_drops %>% dplyr::filter(status != "retained")

## remove failing samples (blanks / controls untouched)
dat_filt_taxa_df <- dat_filt_taxa_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(samp_keep, minboot, sample_id, keep),
                   by = c("minboot", "sample_id")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(type != "sample" | keep) %>%
  dplyr::select(-keep)
```

```{r set_mins_divs}
  summarise(min_sample=min(sum_sample), low_quant=quantile(sum_sample, probs=0.25), seventyfivepercent_lower=0.75*low_quant, fiftypercent_lower=0.50*low_quant, low_10percent=quantile(sum_sample, probs=0.10), median=median(sum_sample), mean=mean(sum_sample),num_samp=n(),samp_below_quant= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<low_quant]), samp_below_75= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<seventyfivepercent_lower]), samp_below_50= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<fiftypercent_lower]), samp_below_10p= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<low_10percent]))
#   !!!!!!!!! take a look, most in cores have very low rare to 3000 remove any sample less than 1000
# Feb 2021, try to automate rarefy decision.....
#  seems like fair trade off between being too stringent for min. reads and removing samples with fewer reads than min ..
#   use lower quartile (75% of samples) for minimum for rarefaction and then remove 10% of samples with low reads.
##  this results in about 10% samples removed and 10% of samples have reads below rarefaction minumum.
```

```{r rar_and_div}
  #  x<-rar2[[12]]
```

```{r summary_table}
#################### makes summary tables to then be exported
# names(filter_summary_per_primer_minboot)

pm <- function(m, se) sprintf("%.0f \u00b1 %.0f", m, se)   # mean ± SE in one cell

## DADA2 steps are the same for every minboot, so one row per primer x eDNA type
DADA<-filter_summary_per_primer_minboot %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    distinct(primers,eDNA, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
    transmute(primers, eDNA,
      `Reads: primers removed`   = pm(primer_removed_mean, primer_removed_se),
      `Reads: quality filtered`  = pm(filtered_mean, filtered_se),
      `Reads: denoised`          = pm(denoised_mean, denoised_se),
      `Reads: pairs merged`      = pm(FandR_merged_mean, FandR_merged_se),
      `Reads: chimeras removed`  = pm(bimeras_removed_mean, bimeras_removed_se)) %>% 
   arrange(primers, desc(eDNA) )
DADA_footnote <- "Per-sample mean \u00b1 SE of reads remaining after each DADA2 step, in pipeline order."
  

## per-sample mean ± SE at each filtering step, in pipeline order
## (1) 97% cluster in >= min_samples_include samples; (2) 97% cluster >= sam_sum_prop_cut of
## total sample reads; (3) taxonomy assigned at class level or below;
## (4) contaminants removed: decontam combined (threshold 0.1) OR (in >= blank_n_remove blanks
##     with share of blank reads >= blank_ratio_min x share of sample reads);
## (5) ASVs summed within taxon x 97% cluster
post_DADA_sum <- filter_summary_per_primer_minboot %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(primers, taxa_assign, eDNA,
      `Reads: occurrence filter`        = pm(after_n_occurance_per_sample_mean, after_n_occurance_per_sample_se),
      `Reads: cluster read cutoff`       = pm(after_min_sample_filt_mean, after_min_sample_filt_se),
      `Reads: taxonomy assigned`         = pm(after_taxa_clean_mean, after_taxa_clean_se),
      `Reads: contaminants removed`      = pm(after_blank_filt_mean, after_blank_filt_se),
      `Reads: non-marine removed`        = pm(after_marine_filt_mean, after_marine_filt_se),
      `ASVs: occurrence filter`         = pm(SV_after_n_occurance_mean, SV_after_n_occurance_se),
      `ASVs: cluster read cutoff`        = pm(SV_after_min_sample_filt_mean, SV_after_min_sample_filt_se),
      `ASVs: taxonomy assigned`          = pm(SV_after_taxa_clean_mean, SV_after_taxa_clean_se),
      `ASVs: contaminants removed`       = pm(SV_after_blank_filt_mean, SV_after_blank_filt_se),
      `ASVs: non-marine removed`         = pm(SV_after_marine_filt_mean, SV_after_marine_filt_se),
      `Taxonomic units (taxon x cluster)` = pm(SV_after_taxa_sum_mean, SV_after_taxa_sum_se)) %>%
   arrange(primers, desc(taxa_assign), desc(eDNA))

post_DADA_footnote <- sprintf(paste0(
  "Per-sample mean \u00b1 SE. Steps in order: 97%% clusters (DECIPHER, 3%% cutoff) present in ",
  ">= %d samples; clusters with >= %s of total sample reads per primer; taxonomy assigned ",
  "(bootstrap >= %s) at class level or below; contaminants removed with decontam ",
  "(combined method, threshold 0.1) or present in >= %d blanks with a larger share of blank than of sample reads; ",
  "non-marine / terrestrial taxa removed (%d rules); ASVs summed by taxon within 97%% clusters. ",
  "Means include all sequenced samples; samples with < %d reads after these steps were then removed%s."),
  min_samples_include, format(sam_sum_prop_cut, scientific = FALSE), minboots_summary, blank_n_remove,
  nrow(non_marine), sample_read_cut, if (require_both_primers) " (a sample must pass for both primers)" else "")
```

```{r export_1}
## tab_df() ignores `file =` when knitting, so write the HTML explicitly
## publication primer labels (primer pair -> 18S region) in cells and column names;
## internal names (18smini, euka02) are kept in the data export for the analysis script
pub_primer <- c("18smini" = "18S_V9", "euka02" = "18S_V7")
pub_lab <- function(x) {
  for (k in names(pub_primer)) x <- gsub(k, pub_primer[[k]], x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}
save_tab <- function(df, file, ...) {
  df <- as.data.frame(df)
  names(df) <- pub_lab(names(df))
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(v) if (is.character(v) || is.factor(v)) pub_lab(as.character(v)) else v)
  tb <- sjPlot::tab_df(df, alternateRowColors = FALSE, describe = FALSE, ...)
  writeLines(tb$page.complete, file, useBytes = TRUE)
  tb
}

save_tab(DADA, paste0(dir, summary_file, "DADA2_read_summary.html"), digits = 0,
         footnote = DADA_footnote, show.footnote = TRUE)

save_tab(post_DADA_sum, paste0(dir, summary_file, "Post_DADA2_read_summary.html"), digits = 0,
         footnote = post_DADA_footnote, show.footnote = TRUE)

save_tab(post_DADA_totals, paste0(dir, summary_file, "Post_DADA2_totals_summary.html"), digits = 0,
         title = "Total ASVs, clusters and taxonomic units per primer")

save_tab(post_DADA_contam, paste0(dir, summary_file, "Post_DADA2_contam_summary.html"), digits = 2,
```

## Replicate analysis
Extraction replicates (separate DNA extractions of the same sediment sample; each
extract amplified as a pool of 5 PCRs, as for every sample): DC 2016 C2 (2 extractions),
CCF_S 2017 FB CR1 (2) and CCF_S 2017 YB CR2 (3). Replicates are kept in the export but excluded from all analyses
(`!grepl("rep", sample_id)` in the analysis script). Diagnostic only; minboot 70.

Findings (2026-10-24, current filter settings):

- Reproducibility between extractions of the same sample is variable. Bray-Curtis between
  replicates (18S_V9 / 18S_V7): C2 0.33 / 0.30; FB 0.64 / 0.30; YB CR2 vs its two
  replicates 0.79, 0.77 / 0.35, 0.61; YB rep2 vs rep3 0.20 / 0.42. Median for any two
  samples: 0.62. C2 replicates are each other's closest sample of all 73 (next closest
  0.40 / 0.49) and the two YB replicates are close to each other, but the FB and YB
  originals can differ from their replicates as much as two unrelated samples,
  especially for 18S_V9.
- The poorly matching extracts are low in DNA (extract conc FB CR1 0.026 vs replicate
  0.103, YB CR2 0.162, YB replicates < 0.5 ng/ml; C2 0.27 / 0.44, the highest). Because
  each extract is already a pool of 5 PCRs, most of the difference is likely sediment
  heterogeneity between subsamples (patchy DNA, worse when DNA is scarce) rather than PCR.
- Low-abundance detections reproduce poorly. Pooled over all 5 pairs, % of taxa in one
  replicate also found in the other (expected from read sampling alone in brackets):
  < 0.01% of reads 42-46% (72-73%); 0.01-0.1% 55-56% (98-100%); 0.1-1% 75-78% (100%);
  > 1% 77-87% (100%). Above 0.1%: C2 94-98%, other pairs 53-97%.
- Implications: (1) a single extraction per sample carries a lot of noise, which limits how much
  variation habitat can explain (PERMANOVA R2 ~5-7%); (2) detections < 0.1% are mostly not
  reproducible, supporting the optional presence threshold `pa_min_pct` in the analysis
  script's `community_matrix`; (3) even abundant taxa are not always reproduced, so
  per-sample composition should be interpreted at the community / habitat level.
- Related checks (scratch, not in the scripts): with a 0.1% per-sample presence cut the
  taxa found in all three habitats drop from 78% to 35%, but habitat R2 barely changes
  (0.057 -> 0.054): low-abundance detections inflate apparent overlap (Venns) without
  hiding a habitat signal. 18S_V7 separates habitats slightly better than 18S_V9 (R2
  0.068 vs 0.050). Habitat stays significant after latitude/longitude (R2 0.063,
  p = 0.002); nearby (< 5 km) between-habitat pairs differ more than same-habitat pairs.

```{r rep_anal}
## replicate IDs lack the original's number; originals identified from old_sample_ID
## (extract concentration label) in the sample sheet: YB CR_rep2 and YB CR _rep3 =
## "CCF_S 2017 0.932" = YB CR2; FB CR_rep2 = "0.964" = FB CR1; C2_rep2 = "C2 eDNA" = C2.
## (sample_data sheet calls the YB replicate "YB CR1_rep2" but its station is CR2.)
rep_sets <- list(
  C2  = c("DC 2016 C2", "DC 2016 C2_rep2"),
  FB  = c("CCF_S 2017 FB CR1", "CCF_S 2017 FB CR_rep2"),
  YBa = c("CCF_S 2017 YB CR2", "CCF_S 2017 YB CR_rep2"),
  YBb = c("CCF_S 2017 YB CR2", "CCF_S 2017 YB CR _rep3"),
  YBc = c("CCF_S 2017 YB CR_rep2", "CCF_S 2017 YB CR _rep3"))

rep_dat <- dat_filt_taxa_df2 %>%   # = exported RS_surface_filtered_data_all.csv.gz
  filter(minboot == 70, type == "sample", primer %in% c("18smini", "euka02")) %>%
  mutate(sample_id = trimws(sample_id),
         primer    = dplyr::recode(primer, "18smini" = "18S_V9", "euka02" = "18S_V7"),
         lineage   = stringr::str_replace(lineage, ";-?\\d+$", "")) %>%
  group_by(primer, sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(reads = sum(reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(reads > 0) %>%
  group_by(primer, sample_id) %>%
  mutate(depth = sum(reads), pct = reads / depth) %>%
  ungroup()

rep_out <- list(); rep_bc <- list()
for (pr in c("18S_V9", "18S_V7")) {
  w <- rep_dat %>% filter(primer == pr) %>%
    select(sample_id, lineage, pct) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = lineage, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample_id") %>% as.matrix()
  bc <- as.matrix(vegan::vegdist(sqrt(w), "bray"))
  not_rep <- rownames(bc)[!grepl("rep", rownames(bc))]
  med_all <- median(bc[not_rep, not_rep][upper.tri(bc[not_rep, not_rep])])

  for (nm in names(rep_sets)) {
    ids <- rep_sets[[nm]]
    rep_bc[[length(rep_bc) + 1]] <- tibble(primer = pr, set = nm, bray_replicates = round(bc[ids[1], ids[2]], 2),
      bray_median_all_samples = round(med_all, 2),
      closest_other_sample = names(sort(bc[ids[2], setdiff(not_rep, ids)]))[1])
    ## each detection in one replicate: found in the other? vs expected from read sampling
    for (k in 1:2) {
      a <- filter(rep_dat, primer == pr, sample_id == ids[k])
      b <- filter(rep_dat, primer == pr, sample_id == ids[3 - k])
      rep_out[[length(rep_out) + 1]] <- tibble(primer = pr, set = nm, pct = a$pct,
        found = a$lineage %in% b$lineage, expected = 1 - exp(-a$pct * b$depth[1]))
    }
  }
}

## similarity of replicates vs all samples
bind_rows(rep_bc)

## reproducibility by abundance class, all pairs pooled, then per pair
rep_out <- bind_rows(rep_out) %>%
  mutate(abund = cut(100 * pct, c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 100),
                     labels = c("< 0.01%", "0.01-0.1%", "0.1-1%", "> 1%")),
         set = factor(set, levels = names(rep_sets)))
rep_out %>%
  group_by(primer, abund) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), found_in_pair = round(100 * mean(found)),
            expected_read_sampling = round(100 * mean(expected)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(primer, abund)

## per pair: % of detections found in the other replicate, below / above 0.1% of reads
rep_out %>%
  mutate(abund2 = if_else(pct >= 0.001, ">= 0.1%", "< 0.1%")) %>%
  group_by(set, primer, abund2) %>%
  summarise(found_in_pair = round(100 * mean(found)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(primer, abund2), values_from = found_in_pair)
```
